intro:
You may have searched for something like "running shoes" on Google and noticed photos of shoes with prices sitting right at the top of the results, above the normal links. Those are PLAs.

PLA stands for Product Listing Ads. They are Google's shopping ads, the ones that show a picture, a price, and the name of the store next to each product. If you sell physical products online, these ads are one of the most direct ways to get in front of buyers who are ready to spend money.

In this post I will explain what PLAs are in plain language, how they differ from regular Google Ads, and what it takes to run them for your own store.

body: When you search for a product on Google, the results page often starts with a row or carousel of product listings. Each one shows a photo, the product name, the price, and which store sells it. Those listings are paid ads, and the format is called Product Listing Ads.

They used to be a separate ad type, and the name stuck even though Google now groups them under Shopping ads. Either way, the idea is the same: your products appear visually, with prices, in front of people who are actively shopping.
sections.heading: What PLA Means in Plain English

body: Regular Google Ads are text ads. You write the headline and the description, you pick the keywords, and your ad shows up as a few lines of text.

PLAs work differently. You do not write ad copy at all. Google builds the ads automatically from your product feed, which is a file containing your product titles, descriptions, prices, images, and stock levels. Google then matches your products to relevant searches on its own.

This is both the strength and the challenge of PLAs. You cannot bid on individual keywords the way you can with text ads, but you also do not have to write dozens of ad variations. The quality of your product data does most of the heavy lifting.
sections.heading: How PLAs Differ From Regular Google Ads

body: Because PLAs show a photo and a price before anyone clicks, the people who do click are already interested in what you are selling. They have seen what the product looks like and what it costs, so the curiosity clicks are filtered out before you pay for them.

That pre-qualification is why shopping ads often convert better than text ads for ecommerce stores. A shopper comparing three listings side by side can pick yours based on the image and the price, then land directly on the product page.
For small stores this is a big advantage. You compete on the product and the price, not on who writes the cleverest ad headline.
sections.heading: Why PLAs Work So Well for Online Stores

body: To run PLAs you need three things connected together: a Google Merchant Center account, a product feed, and a Google Ads account. The Merchant Center is free. It holds your product data and applies Google's shopping policies to your listings.

The product feed is the critical piece. It should include clear product titles, accurate prices, high-quality images on a clean background, and correct availability. Stores that treat the feed like an afterthought get weak results. Stores that polish their titles and images get more clicks for the same spend.
If your store runs on Shopify or WooCommerce, there are free tools and apps that generate the feed automatically and keep it updated when you change a price or sell out an item.
sections.heading: What You Need to Run Product Listing Ads

body: PLAs are built for physical products. If you sell anything a customer can hold, wear, or use at home, shopping ads fit. Clothing, electronics, furniture, supplements, parts, and gifts all perform well in this format.
Service businesses get less from PLAs because there is no product to photograph and price. If you sell services, text ads and organic search are better places to spend.

Local shops with online stores should not ignore PLAs either. Google can show your products to people searching near your location, including whether the item is in stock at your store. That bridges your online and walk-in traffic nicely.
sections.heading: Which Businesses Should Use PLAs

body: Start with your best sellers, not your full catalog. Pick ten to twenty products with good margins and clean photos, get the feed right, and watch the results for a few weeks before expanding.

Keep titles specific and honest. A title like "Men's Waterproof Hiking Boots, Brown Leather, Size 9" will match better searches than "Great Boots." Google reads your titles to decide which searches deserve your ads.

Watch the search terms report in Google Ads. It shows the actual searches that triggered your ads. If irrelevant searches keep appearing, add them as negative keywords or fix the product titles that caused the mismatch.

Finally, remember that PLAs and SEO work well together. Products that rank organically still benefit from the extra visibility of shopping ads above them, and the feed work you do improves how your products appear everywhere.
